content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I need some assistance. I'm working with a [product_name] with [article_no] and require one analog input. In the hardware settings, I've configured for two analog inputs using channels I7 and I8. My analog device is connected to I7. The issue is that I'm running out of digital inputs (I need seven in total) and would rather not buy an expansion module if possible. Is it feasible to use I8 as a digital input while I7 stays analog? Will the [product_name] automatically detect a high/low signal on I8 and handle it appropriately, or are both inputs reserved only for analog once configured? I hope this is clear. Any advice would be appreciated. Thank you.

Yes, you can use one of the two analog inputs as a digital input. There's no extra setup required for this, everything works as expected. You just need to choose whether to use I7 or I8 as the analog input. It's technically possible to use an input as both analog and digital in your program. In most cases, the program won't operate reliably, but if you're experienced with [product_name], you could multiplex the signal: for one second use I7 as digital input and store its state, then the next second use I7 as analog input, alternating accordingly. You can save the analog measurement in a math function at the intervals when it's used as a digital input.

analysis.insight_summary: A user was unsure whether analog/digital inputs on [product_name] could be flexibly utilized. The discussion clarified that automatic recognition of digital signals on analog inputs is possible, and configuration options impact input usage. There is some uncertainty about reliability when multiplexing analog and digital functions on a single input, though advanced programming might make it feasible.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to configure one channel for analog sensing and another for digital use on the available hardware, ideally combining both functions without needing to buy additional modules.
